Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Pinnacle Asset Management Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question during this time, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, please press star then two. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Pinnacle Asset Management's Q3 2024 results. Joining me on today's call are David Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Emily Carter, Chief Financial Officer; and Michael Reyes, Chief Investment Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to David Thompson.

David Thompson: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q3 2024. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by the successful rollout of innovative new strategies and exceptional fund rankings that propelled organic assets under management growth and client inflows, even against a tough backdrop of sticky inflation, geopolitical strains, and the Federal Reserve's commitment to elevated rates for an extended period.

To elaborate, we saw tremendous traction with three major product introductions in the quarter, designed to meet shifting investor needs around thematic investing, downside protection, and long-term sustainability. Leading the pack was our Pinnacle AI & Robotics ETF, ticker PAIR, a passive vehicle tracking our custom index of 150 top global players in AI, machine learning, and robotics. It debuted on April 15th and pulled in $750 million in net inflows in just the first two months, surpassing our $500 million goal, thanks to keen interest from pension plans and registered investment advisors shifting away from generic tech benchmarks like the Nasdaq-100. With an ultra-competitive expense ratio of 0.18%, it features significant allocations to U.S. heavyweights such as NVIDIA and TSMC, which together make up 25%, plus European standouts like ASML and rising stars in Asia Pacific including Samsung Electronics. Initial returns have impressed, with 12.4% gains since launch compared to 8.2% for the MSCI World Tech Index, powered by our forward-focused emphasis on generative AI technologies.

Building on that momentum, we launched the Pinnacle Climate Transition Bond Fund, an actively managed fixed-income offering aiming for $1 billion in assets by December. It focuses on green, social, and sustainability-linked bonds from companies and governments demonstrably shifting to lower-carbon operations, prioritizing investment-grade corporates and sovereign debt. We've already locked in $420 million from European wealth platforms and U.S. endowments, riding the wave of the EU's Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation and demand for Article 8 and 9 classified funds. We keep duration prudent at 5.2 years, delivering a yield to worst of 4.8%, while targeting a 40% drop in carbon intensity relative to the Bloomberg Global Aggregate Bond Index. Our edge comes from an in-house ESG analytics tool using machine learning on satellite data and supply chains to sidestep heavy polluters like oil and gas, yielding a backtested Sharpe ratio of 1.45.

Rounding out the trio, our alternatives lineup advanced with the Pinnacle Private Credit Opportunities Fund II, which wrapped up its initial institutional close at $2.2 billion, oversubscribed 1.7 times by a broad mix of family offices and Middle Eastern sovereign wealth funds. This perpetual structure goes after senior direct loans to middle-market firms in sturdy sectors such as healthcare and tech services in the U.S. and Europe, eyeing net IRRs of 10-12% with loan-to-value limits at 55%. So far, 28% of capital is deployed at spreads averaging SOFR plus 550 basis points, capitalizing on turbulence in syndicated loans.

Geographically, these efforts highlight our worldwide reach: U.S. new assets accounted for 55% or $1.9 billion, Europe 30% at $1.0 billion thanks to UCITS wrappers, and APAC 15% or $500 million, strong in Japan and Australia amid currency pressures and pension shifts. This spread reduces reliance on any single market and sets us up for the anticipated $5 trillion surge in global alternatives by 2028, according to Preqin.

Emily Carter: Thank you, David. From a financial perspective, Pinnacle Asset Management delivered strong results in Q3 2024. Our revenue was $1.42 billion, representing a 12% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by sustained strength in our management fee revenue and average fee rate dynamics, forming the core of our predictable earnings stream in a fiercely competitive field.

Diving deeper, management fees hit $852 million for the quarter, rising 8% from last year and 5% from Q2. This stemmed from healthy AUM buildup and steady net inflows, tempered somewhat by fee pressures I'll detail. Over the first nine months, fees reached $2.51 billion, a healthy 10% gain versus prior year, proving our model's toughness amid industry challenges like rate squeezes and swings.

Total AUM closed at $1.55 trillion, up 12% year-over-year and 4% linked-quarter. Markets contributed about 7%, especially in equities and balanced portfolios with the S&P 500's robust YTD advance, plus $25 billion in organic inflows, or 1.6% of beginning balances. Twelve-month long-term flows are now $95 billion, spanning institutional and retail, with passives and ETFs grabbing $45 billion and alts $20 billion.

Average fee rates stood at 52 basis points, off 2 bps from last year. This tracks peer patterns at firms like BlackRock and Vanguard, as low-cost indexing gains ground. Breakdown: equities 48 bps down 1 bp, fixed income 35 bps steady, multi-asset 55 bps up 1 bp on composition, alts 85 bps up 3 bps from private credit and infra scaling.

The dip largely reflects mix: passives like our ETF and index lineup now 45% of AUM, versus 38% last year, with fees around 12 bps, sharp against rivals like Vanguard's VTI at 3 bps or our S&P tracker at 5 bps. Excluding mix, rates held near 53.5 bps. Institutional bids also push tiered pricing, trimming 50-75 bps on mandates over $5 billion.

By region, Americas at 60% AUM saw fees up 11% to $510 million on $18 billion retirement flows into target-dates and models, fees firm at 51 bps from active equities in DB plans. EMEA fees grew 6% to $210 million but rates to 49 bps on UCITS ETFs like our Euro Stoxx 50 at 10 bps and $15 billion AUM under MiFID II scrutiny. APAC shone with 15% fee rise to $132 million on $12 billion flows from Gulf SWFs and Aussie/Japanese retail, fees at 58 bps on active Asia ex-Japan and privates amid yen slides and infra demand.

We're countering proactively: ramped passive expansion with three active ETFs like Pinnacle Active ESG Equity and smart-beta packs at 25-35 bps for the $10 trillion ETF arena growing 12% CAGR per Morningstar. Our Aligned Wealth robo-hybrid added 150,000 clients and $3 billion AUM at 40 bps, upselling direct indexing at 60-75 bps for high-net-worth. In alts, Pinnacle Credit Opportunities IV hit $12 billion for 110 bps yield, infra $8 billion tapping $1.5 trillion dry powder.

For Q4, we see fees up 7-9% YoY at $1.6 trillion AUM assuming steady markets and $20-25 billion flows, rates at 51-52 bps. Our 60/40 active/passive balance, channel diversity, and $500 million tech spend position us ahead of peers like T. Rowe or Fidelity on flows.

Our expenses were $950 million, resulting in net income of $320 million. We continue to manage our expenses prudently while investing in key growth initiatives. Before passing to Michael, let me outline our full-year 2024 outlook and Q4 specifics, assuming no big macro disruptions, stable markets, and ongoing flows. Amid U.S. equities' 18% YTD resilience and cooling inflation, but watchful of rate cuts and global tensions.

Full-year revenue: $5.45 billion to $5.65 billion, 12-16% above 2023's $4.85 billion. AUM eyed at $1.40-$1.45 trillion end-year, 14-18% growth from $1.23 trillion. Using 38 bps average fees steady despite passive drag.

Management/advisory (85%): $4.65-$4.80 billion on AUM rise. Flows $85-$95 billion full-year, beating prior $75 billion: $45 billion ETFs like Pinnacle Core Equity mimicking IVV scale with 2.5% U.S. share on AI boom, $30 billion retirement/wealth, $12 billion active equities/alts with perf fees from quant long-short beating HFRI by 450 bps Q3.

Performance fees (8%): $420-$480 million, +25% YoY, from alts hurdles in $150 billion platform like Sustainable Infra at 12-15% IRR for $250 million.

Distribution/other (7%): $370-$390 million, boosted by sub-advisory and Model Delivery up 30% via RIA ties.

U.S. (70% AUM) 75% growth from DC wins/$10 billion 401(k)s; EMEA 10% on ESG ETFs vs. Amundi/DWS; APAC 20% on $8 billion Japan ETF/China feeders.

Markets add $120 billion (8% MSCI beta), alts to 11% AUM, robo Aether Direct $25 billion at 25 bps.

Expenses: $3.75-$3.90 billion, expense/revenue 67-69%, margins 28-30%. Up 9% YoY.

Comp/benefits (55%): $2.05-$2.15 billion +10%, variable +18% on ROA/AUM. PM bonuses 120% base on macro fund +12% vs. HFRX +4%.

G&A (20%): $750-$775 million flat ex-inflation, via India services -8% back-office.

Marketing/distribution/tech (25%): $950 million-$1.075 billion +15%: $250 million AI/data incl. GenAI optimizer/Aladdin upgrade cutting alpha decay 20%; $300 million wholesalers (450 FTEs)/digital for $20 billion RIA; $150 million SEC T+1/MiFID III.

Q4 higher on $50 million tech one-offs, but 200 bps margin gain on flows.

Tailwinds: alts democratization $15 trillion TAM by 2030 per Cerulli, three active ETFs. Derisked with 40% cash, 20% FI hedges. Risks: yield spikes, fee wars, APAC regs, countered by $12 billion PE powder, 22% capital.

Michael Reyes: Thank you, Emily. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities and fixed income. We are navigating the current market environment by leveraging our performance edge across over 1,200 funds, where 68% of AUM sits in top-quartile performers per Morningstar, Lipper, and Russell over the year to June 30th. We added 47 fresh five-star Morningstar ratings in Q3, totaling 162 funds covering 42% of rated equity AUM and 35% of fixed income, improved from 38% and 31% a year prior.

Highlights include the Pinnacle Large Cap Growth Fund, ticker PLCGX, holding five stars and 8th percentile in its Large Growth category, producing 2.3% alpha to the S&P 500 with 15% lower volatility via quant stock picks using earnings sentiment data.

Equities: 72% active outperformance net fees, international small-cap ace with Pinnacle Emerging Markets Small Cap at +18.7% vs. MSCI EM Small Cap +14.2%, riding India/Indonesia shifts away from China. Fixed income: core bonds +5.2% YTD beating Barclays Agg by 120 bps, short-duration/munis earning four/five-star Lipper on 85% AUM. Multi-asset target-dates: 91% top-half, suiting DC de-risking.

This stems from our three pillars: AlphaForge AI optimizer tilting factors across 5,000 securities for 65 bps excess YTD; ESG in 55% AUM, outpacing non-ESG by 180 bps in volatility; 92% PM retention at 12+ years for process consistency.

Forward, H2 favors bond duration on cuts, AI themes, privates premiums with CAPE at 35x. Supports 8-10% organic AUM to $1.2 trillion, $5 billion more launches.

David Thompson: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes our targeted mergers and acquisitions, a cornerstone of inorganic expansion amid fee pressures averaging 15 bps compression in active equities per Morningstar, and evolving demands for alts and ESG.

We completed two tuck-ins in Q3, netting $28.4 billion AUM to hit pro forma $1.2 trillion, 12% inorganic growth countering $4.2 billion long-only equity outflows on growth rotations.

First, Horizon Sustainable Partners, $16.7 billion London ESG boutique excelling in SFDR Article 8/9, Europe small-cap sustainable equities +18% annualized vs. MSCI 9%, green bonds 4.2% yield. Closed at 14x forward FRE, below BlackRock/GIP 20x, funded $450 million cash/2.1 million shares at 5% discount.

Boosts Europe ESG share to 22% top-10 per eVestment. Synergies ahead of $35 million run-rate: 60% UCITS on our Aladdin platform -8 bps TER, 97% retention, $1.2 billion U.S. cross-sell. Europe M&A +25% YoY per PwC on MiFID/Sfdr; two more in pipeline.

Second, Pacific Alpha Strategies, $11.7 billion Singapore quant alts, APAC long-short equity/credit, flagship +12.4% vs. HFRI Asia ex-Japan +550 bps via ML vol targeting. $320 million/12.5x EBITDA, lifts alts to 18% AUM for mid-teens revenue.

APAC AUM +22% CAGR since 2020 on SWFs to 40% alts. Integrate signals to sys equities, $2 billion U.S. wirehouse pilot, Tokyo feeders. $25 million integration, +150 bps fees/10% savings via State Street.

Pipeline: $150 billion targets—U.S. FI boutiques on bond rotation, ETF passive, APAC/Europe priv credit on $1.5 trillion powder. Opportunistic at 10-15x FRE, >20% IRR, 60/40 debt/equity.

"Scale via specialization": top managers grab 65% flows per BCG, M&A adds 200-300 bps ROA in 18 months. YTD 8% of 11% AUM growth, $185 million rev run-rate, 120 pros added.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more details on the management fee revenue trends and how you're addressing fee compression?

David Thompson: Good morning, John. Absolutely, as Emily detailed, our management fees grew 8% year-over-year to $852 million, supported by AUM expansion and resilient flows. We're countering compression through higher-margin alts and tech like direct indexing, keeping the blended rate stable on a mix-adjusted basis.

John Smith: Thank you. And a follow-up on the revenue and expense guidance for the full year?

Emily Carter: Thanks, John. We're guiding full-year revenue to $5.45-$5.65 billion and expenses to $3.75-$3.90 billion, with margins expanding to 28-30%. This assumes continued flows and market stability, with investments in AI and distribution driving long-term efficiency.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of the Pinnacle Private Credit Opportunities Fund II?

Michael Reyes: Good morning, Lisa. The fund closed its first tranche at $2.2 billion, oversubscribed, and has deployed 28% of capital at SOFR +550 bps spreads to resilient mid-market borrowers. It's on track for 10-12% net IRR, benefiting from syndicated loan disruptions, with strong LP commitment from family offices and SWFs.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to David Thompson for closing remarks.

David Thompson: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Pinnacle Asset Management. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
